turns: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
results.answer: Minneapolis (MSP) is the Midwest hub most exposed to winter disruption, with a winter score of 48.2. That is still only moderate in absolute terms. Chicago (39.9) and Detroit (37.4) follow, also moderate, and Kansas City is at 33.8, just inside moderate. Indianapolis (30.7) and Columbus (30.1) are low. No Midwest hub reaches the high band (66 or above). MSP's main drivers are 146.4 freeze days/yr (min temp <= 0 C) and 20.4 days/yr with snowfall >= 1 cm. Chicago has 103.6 freeze days and 18.6 snow days/yr. Detroit has 111.4 freeze days and 17.0 snow days/yr.

turns: Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
results.answer: Miami has higher hurricane/wind exposure, and Houston has much higher flood exposure. Wind: Miami scores 51.9 (moderate) and Houston 43.1 (moderate). The gap comes mainly from FEMA wind declarations, 11 for Miami and 8 for Houston over 20 years. Gust days are similar: 11.8 days/yr at 60 km/h or more for Miami and 10.8 for Houston. Flood: Houston scores 74.7 (high) and Miami 32.4 (low). Houston has 23.6 days/yr with 25 mm or more of rain, against 9.2 for Miami. It also has 4.2 days/yr at 50 mm or more (Miami 2.2) and 7 FEMA flood declarations (Miami 2). Composite scores are 39.0 for Houston and 22.7 for Miami. Only Houston's flood score is high in absolute terms. Both hubs are moderate on wind.

turns: What percentage of days in Denver last year had snowfall?
results.answer: In 2025, Denver had measurable snowfall (at least 0.1 cm) on 37 of 365 days, which is 10.1% of days. Snowfall of at least 1 cm occurred on 17 days, or 4.7%.

Heat adds 6.8 points, from 54.6 days/yr at or above 35 C. Winter adds only 3.5 points.

results.answer: The three highest composite scores are Houston (39.0), Dallas (36.5) and Newark (33.4). All three are only "moderate" in absolute terms, because the high band starts at 66. Dallas and Newark are 3.1 points apart, which is just outside it, but the tool flags Newark as a close call with the next hub (the fourth ranked), so Newark's third place is also uncertain.
